records.source: וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן־יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן־עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, went up Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel [to] Jerusalem for battle against it, and not he was able to fight against it.
pieces: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem to make war on it, but they were not able to take it.

L.1: And it was in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, [that] Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up [to] Jerusalem for battle against it, and he was not able to fight against it.

R.1: Ahaz son of Jotham, the grandson of Uzziah, was king of Judah. While he ruled, King Rezin of Aram and King Pekah son of Remaliah, who ruled the northern kingdom of Israel, came to attack Jerusalem. But they could not capture it.

decisions.choice: the attack of Rezin and Pekah on Jerusalem, told also in 2 Kings 16:5
decisions.reason: The opening of the verse matches 2 Kings 16:5 almost word for word. Rezin ruled Aram from Damascus, and Pekah ruled the northern kingdom of Israel from Samaria. The attack came in the 730s BC, while Assyria was pressing west; 2 Kings 16:7-9 and 2 Chronicles 28:5-21 tell how Ahaz answered it by sending for help to the king of Assyria.

decisions.choice: he was not able to fight against it: the attack failed to take the city
alternatives: they could not yet begin the attack on it
decisions.reason: The verse tells the outcome before the story of verses 2-9: the siege did not succeed. "Fight against it" here means to win the battle for it. The verb is singular in the Hebrew text, most likely with the two kings taken together or the leader of the attack in view; 2 Kings 16:5 and the Great Isaiah Scroll have the plural, "they were not able".

decisions.choice: they were not able to take it / they could not capture it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he was not able" refers to the attack of both kings, so Balanced and Readable say "they". Readable also says that Israel here is the northern kingdom, not Judah, and calls Uzziah Ahaz's grandson.

records.heading: Two charred ends of firewood

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נָ֥חָֽה אֲרָ֖ם עַל־אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֤נַע לְבָבוֹ֙ וּלְבַ֣ב עַמּ֔וֹ כְּנ֥וֹעַ עֲצֵי־יַ֖עַר מִפְּנֵי־רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: And it was told to [the] house of David, saying, has settled Aram on Ephraim. And shook his heart and [the] heart of his people, as shake [the] trees of [the] forest before a wind.
pieces: Word came to the house of David: "Aram has camped in Ephraim." Then the king's heart and the hearts of his people shook, like the trees of a forest swaying in the wind.

L.2: And it was told to the house of David, saying, "Aram has settled on Ephraim." And his heart shook, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest shake before a wind.

R.2: Then the royal family of David received this report: "The army of Aram is camped in Ephraim, the land of Israel." King Ahaz and his people were terrified. They shook like trees in a forest when the wind blows.

decisions.choice: Aram has settled on Ephraim: the army of Aram has come to rest in Ephraim's land
decisions.reason: The verb means to come to rest or settle, as the locusts "settled" on Egypt (Exodus 10:14). Here it most likely means that Aram's troops are camped in Ephraim, close to Judah's border. It may instead mean that Aram has joined with Ephraim as an ally; either way the two are acting together against Judah.

decisions.choice: Ephraim: the northern kingdom of Israel
decisions.reason: Ephraim was the leading tribe of the northern kingdom, and Isaiah often uses its name for that whole kingdom (verses 5, 8, 9, 17).

decisions.choice: the house of David ... his heart: the royal house, with Ahaz at its head
decisions.reason: "The house of David" is the reigning family of David's line, to whom God promised a lasting throne (2 Samuel 7:16). "His heart" is the king's, Ahaz's. The shaking trees picture the panic of king and people alike.

decisions.choice: the king's heart / King Ahaz
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his heart"; Balanced and Readable say whose. Readable also says "the army of Aram" and explains that Ephraim is the land of Israel, and it says "terrified" for the shaking heart.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל־יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒ צֵא־נָא֙ לִקְרַ֣את אָחָ֔ז אַתָּ֕ה וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ אֶל־קְצֵ֗ה תְּעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה אֶל־מְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Isaiah, go out please to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, to [the] end of [the] conduit of the pool the upper, to [the] highway of [the] field of [the] washer,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Isaiah, "Take your son Shear-jashub and go out to meet Ahaz at the end of the water channel from the Upper Pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field,

L.3: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Isaiah, "Go out, please, to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, to the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Fuller's Field,

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Isaiah, "Take your son Shear-jashub with you. (His name means 'A remnant will return.') Go out and meet Ahaz at the end of the water channel that comes from the Upper Pool. It is on the road to the field where cloth is washed.

decisions.choice: Shear-jashub: a name meaning "a remnant will return"
decisions.reason: Isaiah's son carries a message in his name, as Isaiah says of his children in 8:18. "A remnant will return" can be heard as a warning (only a remnant will survive) and as a hope (a remnant will come back, or turn back to God). Isaiah 10:20-22 uses the same words in both ways.

decisions.choice: the end of the conduit of the upper pool: the place where the Assyrian envoy later stands
decisions.reason: The same spot is named in 36:2 (and 2 Kings 18:17), where the king of Assyria's commander demands that Hezekiah surrender. Here, at the water channel that served the city, Ahaz is called to trust God; there, his son Hezekiah faces the very power Ahaz turned to.

decisions.choice: the washer's field: where cloth was washed and treated
decisions.reason: A fuller cleaned and thickened new woolen cloth with water, trampling and beating it. The work needed plenty of water, so it was done near a water supply outside the city wall.

decisions.choice: (His name means 'A remnant will return.') ... the field where cloth is washed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of Shear-jashub's name, which is part of the message, and explains the name of the field. Literal and Balanced keep the old name "the Fuller's Field".

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵ֠לָיו הִשָּׁמֵ֨ר וְהַשְׁקֵ֜ט אַל־תִּירָ֗א וּלְבָבְךָ֙ אַל־יֵרַ֔ךְ מִשְּׁנֵ֨י זַנְב֧וֹת הָאוּדִ֛ים הָעֲשֵׁנִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה בָּחֳרִי־אַ֛ף רְצִ֥ין וַאֲרָ֖ם וּבֶן־רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: and you will say to him, take care and be quiet; not fear, and your heart not let be faint from [the] two tails of the firebrands the smoking the these, by [the] heat of [the] anger of Rezin and Aram and [the] son of Remaliah.
pieces: and say to him, 'Watch yourself and keep still. Have no fear. Do not let your courage fail because of these two charred ends of firewood, still smoking: the hot anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.

L.4: and you will say to him, 'Take care and be quiet; do not fear, and let your heart not be faint because of these two tails of smoking firebrands, because of the burning anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.

R.4: Tell him, 'Be careful, and stay calm. Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage because of Rezin of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah. They are angry, but they are like two burned-out sticks that are only smoking. Their fire is almost out.

decisions.choice: two tails of smoking firebrands: two kings whose fire is nearly out
decisions.reason: A firebrand is a stick pulled from the fire. Its "tail" is the burnt stub that is left, giving off smoke but little heat. The two kings look fierce, but their power is almost spent. Within a few years both were gone (verse 16; 2 Kings 15:30; 16:9).

decisions.choice: take care and be quiet: stay on guard, and keep calm in trust
decisions.reason: The first verb means to watch oneself, to be on guard; the second to be still and undisturbed. Ahaz is not to act in panic. Isaiah later says the same to the people: "In quietness and in trust shall be your strength" (30:15).

decisions.choice: the son of Remaliah: Pekah, named only by his father's name
decisions.reason: Isaiah never names Pekah in this chapter (verses 4, 5, 9). Calling a king only "son of" someone may show scorn, as Saul spoke of David as "the son of Jesse" (1 Samuel 20:27-31).

decisions.choice: Pekah ... They are angry, but they are like two burned-out sticks ... Their fire is almost out.
decisions.reason: Readable names Pekah and explains the picture of the smoking stubs in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the image as it stands.

records.source: יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־יָעַ֥ץ עָלֶ֛יךָ אֲרָ֖ם רָעָ֑ה אֶפְרַ֥יִם וּבֶן־רְמַלְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: Because has planned against you Aram evil, Ephraim and [the] son of Remaliah, saying,
pieces: Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted harm against you. They say,

L.5: Because Aram has planned evil against you, [with] Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying,

R.5: Aram, Ephraim, and Pekah son of Remaliah have made evil plans against you. They have said,

decisions.choice: because: the reason given in verses 5-6 leads to God's answer in verse 7
decisions.reason: The sentence runs from verse 5 to verse 7: because Aram and Ephraim have made their plan, the Lord says it will not stand. Their plan is set against God's plan (14:24-27).

decisions.choice: has planned evil against you: has plotted harm
decisions.reason: The verb is used of making plans and giving counsel. The "evil" is the harm they intend for Judah and its king, set out in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a new sentence, without "because"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make verses 5-6 a sentence of their own and show the link to verse 7 with "So" there. Readable names Pekah.

records.source: נַעֲלֶ֤ה בִֽיהוּדָה֙ וּנְקִיצֶ֔נָּה וְנַבְקִעֶ֖נָּה אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וְנַמְלִ֥יךְ מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ אֵ֖ת בֶּן־טָֽבְאַֽל׃ס
records.gloss: Let us go up against Judah and let us terrify it and let us break into it for ourselves, and let us make king a king in its midst, the son of Tabeel.
pieces: "Let us march against Judah and fill it with dread. Let us break through its walls and take it for ourselves, and put a king in it: the son of Tabeel."

L.6: "Let us go up against Judah and let us terrify it, and let us break into it for ourselves, and let us make king a king in its midst, the son of Tabeel,"

R.6: "We will attack Judah and terrify its people. We will break through its walls and take it for ourselves. Then we will make the son of Tabeel king there."

decisions.choice: let us terrify it: fill it with dread
decisions.reason: The verb most likely comes from a root meaning to dread or be in terror, here "make it dread". It may instead come from a root meaning to cut off or tear apart, "let us tear it apart". Either way it describes a fierce attack.

decisions.choice: let us break into it for ourselves: breach its walls and take it
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or break open, used of breaching a city's wall (2 Kings 25:4; 2 Chronicles 32:1). "For ourselves" means to take it over.

decisions.choice: the son of Tabeel: a man otherwise unknown, whom the two kings meant to put on David's throne
decisions.reason: Tabeel means "God is good" (compare Ezra 4:7). The vowels of the Hebrew text give a slightly different form that sounds like "good for nothing", perhaps a mocking twist of the name. Nothing else is known of him. The plan would have ended the line of David's kings, which God had promised to keep (2 Samuel 7:16).

decisions.choice: We will
decisions.reason: Readable says "We will" for the plotting kings' "Let us", which reads more easily.

records.source: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה לֹ֥א תָק֖וּם וְלֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh, not it will stand and not it will be.
pieces: So the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q "It will not stand. It will not come about.

L.7: thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q "It will not stand, and it will not be.

R.7: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q "Their plan will not succeed. It will not happen.

decisions.choice: it will not stand, and it will not be: the plan will fail
decisions.reason: "Stand" means to hold good or come true. The plan of the two kings will not happen. In 8:10 Isaiah says the same of every plan made against God's people, and in 14:24 that what God plans will stand.

decisions.choice: the Lord Yahweh: God's word answers the kings' plan
decisions.reason: God's answer is set directly against the kings' words in verse 6. Isaiah, speaking for God, delivers a word from God within the message he gives Ahaz.

decisions.choice: Their plan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it"; Readable names what "it" is.

records.source: כִּ֣י רֹ֤אשׁ אֲרָם֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְרֹ֥אשׁ דַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק רְצִ֑ין וּבְע֗וֹד שִׁשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה יֵחַ֥ת אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעָֽם׃
records.gloss: For [the] head of Aram [is] Damascus, and [the] head of Damascus [is] Rezin; and in yet sixty and five years will be shattered Ephraim from [being] a people.
pieces: For Aram's head is Damascus, and Damascus's head is Rezin. \q Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be broken apart and cease to be a people.

L.8: For the head of Aram [is] Damascus, and the head of Damascus [is] Rezin. \q And within sixty-five years more Ephraim will be shattered from [being] a people.

R.8: The capital of Aram is Damascus, and the ruler of Damascus is Rezin. \q In sixty-five years Ephraim will be crushed so badly that it will no longer be a nation.

decisions.choice: the head of Aram is Damascus ... Rezin: these kingdoms have only human heads
decisions.reason: Verses 8-9 name the capital and the king of each attacker. The point seems to be that they are only what they are, a city and a man, and no more; Judah has the LORD's promise to the house of David. The verses leave this contrast unspoken.

decisions.choice: within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered: the end of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC, little more than a dozen years later, and its people were carried off (2 Kings 17:6). After that the kings of Assyria settled foreign peoples in the land, as late as the reign of Esarhaddon (2 Kings 17:24; Ezra 4:2), and Ephraim no longer existed as a people. Sixty-five years from Ahaz's time reaches into that later period. The sentence breaks the pattern of the paired lines in verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: capital ... ruler
decisions.reason: "Head" is used in two senses: the chief city of a country and the king of a city. Readable says "capital" and "ruler"; Literal and Balanced keep "head" for both.

records.source: וְרֹ֤אשׁ אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וְרֹ֥אשׁ שֹׁמְר֖וֹן בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ אִ֚ם לֹ֣א תַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּ֖י לֹ֥א תֵאָמֵֽנוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] head of Ephraim [is] Samaria, and [the] head of Samaria [is the] son of Remaliah. If not you believe, surely not you will be established.
pieces: Ephraim's head is Samaria, and Samaria's head is the son of Remaliah. \q If you do not hold firm in trust, you will not be held firm."'"

L.9: And the head of Ephraim [is] Samaria, and the head of Samaria [is] the son of Remaliah. \q If you do not believe, surely you will not be established."'"

R.9: The capital of Ephraim is Samaria, and the ruler of Samaria is Pekah son of Remaliah. \q If you do not trust firmly in God, you will not stand firm."'"

decisions.choice: believe ... be established: a play on one root, to be firm
decisions.reason: Both verbs come from the same root, meaning to be firm or sure. The first means to trust, to hold firm on someone; the second to be made firm, to last. The same verb is used in God's promise to David, "your house and your kingdom shall be made sure" (2 Samuel 7:16). The house of David will stand only if it trusts God.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the house of David
decisions.reason: Both verbs are plural. The warning is addressed not only to Ahaz but to the whole royal house (verses 2, 13).

decisions.choice: you will not be established: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads "neither will you understand" for the second verb. The Hebrew text, with its play on one root, is followed here.

decisions.choice: hold firm in trust ... be held firm / trust firmly ... stand firm
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "firm" to keep the play on one root. Readable supplies "in God", whom the trust is in (verse 11). Readable also names Pekah.

records.source: וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And again Yahweh spoke to Ahaz, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Ahaz once more:

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke again to Ahaz, saying,

decisions.choice: Yahweh spoke again: through Isaiah
decisions.reason: God speaks to Ahaz through the prophet. That is why, after Ahaz answers, Isaiah speaks of "my God" (verse 13). The verse does not say whether this was the same meeting as verses 3-9 or a later one.

records.heading: A sign for Ahaz

records.source: שְׁאַל־לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת מֵעִ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ הַעְמֵ֣ק שְׁאָ֔לָה א֖וֹ הַגְבֵּ֥הַּ לְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: Ask for yourself a sign from with Yahweh your God; make deep [the] request or make high to above.
pieces: "Ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for a sign. Let your request reach down to the depths or up to the heights above."

L.11: "Ask for yourself a sign from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; make the request deep, or make [it] high above."

R.11: "Ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to give you a sign. You may ask for anything, from deep under the earth to high in the sky."

decisions.choice: a sign: something God does to confirm his word
decisions.reason: A sign is an event that shows a promise will come true, as the shadow on the steps did for Hezekiah (38:7-8) and the fleece did for Gideon (Judges 6:36-40). God offers Ahaz a sign that the attack will fail, so that he can trust.

decisions.choice: make the request deep: the vowels of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "make the request deep". The same letters can be read "make it deep, to Sheol", the world of the dead, which gives a closer pair with "high above"; the Septuagint has "into the depth". The meaning is the same either way: any sign at all, from the lowest depths to the heights.

decisions.choice: deep ... high: from the depths to the heights, anything at all
decisions.reason: Naming the two extremes takes in everything between. Ahaz may ask for any sign he chooses.

decisions.choice: You may ask for anything, from deep under the earth to high in the sky.
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two extremes.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז לֹא־אֶשְׁאַ֥ל וְלֹֽא־אֲנַסֶּ֖ה אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Ahaz, not I will ask, and not I will test Yahweh.
pieces: Ahaz replied, "I will make no request, and I will not test {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.12: And Ahaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not test {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.12: But Ahaz said, "No, I will not ask. I do not want to test {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: I will not test Yahweh: a pious-sounding refusal
decisions.reason: Ahaz echoes the law, "You shall not test the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 6:16). But God himself has offered the sign, so to refuse it is to refuse God. 2 Kings 16:7-9 tells that Ahaz had turned instead to the king of Assyria for help.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙ הַלְא֣וֹת אֲנָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י תַלְא֖וּ גַּ֥ם אֶת־אֱלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said, hear please, house of David! [Is it too] little for you to weary men, that you weary also my God?
pieces: Then Isaiah said, "Listen, house of David! Is wearing people out such a small thing to you that you now wear out my God as well?

L.13: And he said, "Hear, please, house of David! [Is it] too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?

R.13: Then Isaiah said, "Listen, you family of David! You make people tired of you. Is that not enough? Now you are making my God tired of you too!

decisions.choice: he said ... my God: Isaiah speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker is Isaiah, who speaks for God. In verse 11 God was "your God" to Ahaz; now Isaiah says "my God". By refusing the sign, Ahaz has set himself apart from the God who offered it.

decisions.choice: house of David ... you: the royal house, addressed in the plural
decisions.reason: From here to verse 14 "you" is plural. Isaiah speaks to Ahaz as the head of David's royal line, the house to which God made his promise (2 Samuel 7:16).

decisions.choice: Isaiah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said"; Balanced and Readable name Isaiah.

records.source: לָ֠כֵן יִתֵּ֨ן אֲדֹנָ֥י ה֛וּא לָכֶ֖ם א֑וֹת הִנֵּ֣ה הָעַלְמָ֗ה הָרָה֙ וְיֹלֶ֣דֶת בֵּ֔ן וְקָרָ֥את שְׁמ֖וֹ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Therefore will give [the] Lord he to you a sign: look, the young woman [is] pregnant and bearing a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.
pieces: Because of this, the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will give all of you a sign: see, the young woman is pregnant; she will give birth to a son and call him by the name Immanuel.

L.14: Therefore the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will give you a sign: look, the young woman [is] pregnant and bearing a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.

R.14: So the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will give you a sign. A young woman is going to have a baby. She will give birth to a son and name him Immanuel, which means 'God is with us.'

decisions.choice: the young woman: a girl or young woman of age to marry
decisions.reason: The word names a young woman who has come of age. It is used of Rebekah before her marriage (Genesis 24:43), who is also called a virgin (24:16); of Moses' sister as a girl (Exodus 2:8); of the young women in the royal court (Song of Songs 6:8); and in "the way of a man with a young woman" (Proverbs 30:19). It does not by itself say whether she is a virgin or married, though it is never clearly used of a married woman. The Septuagint, translated before the time of Jesus, rendered it with a word that usually means "virgin", and Matthew 1:23 quotes that form, seeing the sign fulfilled when Mary, a virgin, gave birth to Jesus. The article "the" may point to a woman Isaiah and the king both knew, or may simply mark her as the one in the sign.

decisions.choice: is pregnant and bearing a son: the time is open
alternatives: will conceive and bear a son
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb "to be" here, so it can mean that she is already pregnant or that she will become pregnant; the Septuagint and Matthew 1:23 read it as future. "She will call" may also be read "you will call"; the Septuagint has "you" and Matthew has "they will call", and the Great Isaiah Scroll has a form that can mean "he will call" or "one will call". In Israel either parent could name a child (Genesis 4:25; 5:29).

decisions.choice: Immanuel: "God with us"
decisions.reason: The name means "God [is] with us", as Matthew 1:23 explains it. It answers the fear of verse 2: God is with his people. The sign belongs to Ahaz's day, for before the child is old enough to choose good and evil, the two kings' land will be deserted (verse 16). It also reaches further: the name returns in 8:8 and 8:10, a child born to rule on David's throne is promised in 9:5-6, and Matthew 1:22-23 says the birth of Jesus fulfilled this word.

decisions.choice: A young woman ... which means 'God is with us'
decisions.reason: Readable says "a young woman", since the reader is not told who she is; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew "the". Readable also gives the meaning of the name. Balanced says "all of you" because "you" is plural, the house of David.

records.source: חֶמְאָ֥ה וּדְבַ֖שׁ יֹאכֵ֑ל לְדַעְתּ֛וֹ מָא֥וֹס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָח֥וֹר בַּטּֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: Curds and honey he will eat, by his knowing to reject in the evil and to choose in the good.
pieces: Curds and honey will be his food by the time he can turn away from what is bad and choose what is good.

L.15: Curds and honey he will eat, at his knowing to reject the evil and choose the good.

R.15: By the time he is old enough to know right from wrong, he will be eating curds and honey.

decisions.choice: curds and honey: the food of a land that has gone back to pasture
alternatives: rich food, a sign of plenty
decisions.reason: Curds are thickened milk. Verses 21-22 explain them here: with fields left unworked, the few people who remain live on milk from their animals and honey from wild bees, not on grain and wine. Some read the food instead as a sign of plenty, like the "land flowing with milk and honey" (Exodus 3:8). In verses 21-22 it seems to be both: plenty for the few left in an emptied land.

decisions.choice: to reject the evil and choose the good: the age when a child can tell right from wrong
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the early years when a child begins to know good from bad (compare Deuteronomy 1:39). It sets a short time, a few years at most.

decisions.choice: by his knowing: by the time he knows
alternatives: so that he will know how to
decisions.reason: The preposition most likely marks time, "when he knows" or "by the time he knows". It can also mean purpose, "so that he will know".

records.source: כִּ֠י בְּטֶ֨רֶם יֵדַ֥ע הַנַּ֛עַר מָאֹ֥ס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָחֹ֣ר בַּטּ֑וֹב תֵּעָזֵ֤ב הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה קָ֔ץ מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י מְלָכֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: For before knows the boy to reject in the evil and to choose in the good, will be forsaken the land which you [are] dreading from before [the] two of its kings.
pieces: Even before the boy is able to turn from what is bad and choose what is good, the land of those two kings who frighten you will be abandoned.

L.16: For before the boy knows to reject the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you dread will be forsaken.

R.16: Before the boy is old enough to know right from wrong, the lands of the two kings you are so afraid of will be empty.

decisions.choice: the land of the two kings will be forsaken: Aram and Israel laid waste
decisions.reason: Within a few years Assyria took Damascus and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:9, in 732 BC), and took Galilee and Gilead from Israel and carried their people away (2 Kings 15:29). Soon after, Pekah was murdered (2 Kings 15:30).

decisions.choice: the land whose two kings you dread: Aram and Israel taken together
decisions.reason: "The land" is singular, the territory of the two allied kings seen as one. "You" is now singular: Ahaz, who is in dread of them.

decisions.choice: the lands
decisions.reason: Readable says "lands" because two countries are meant.

records.source: יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל־עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ יָמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־בָ֔אוּ לְמִיּ֥וֹם סוּר־אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֑ה אֵ֖ת מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃פ
records.gloss: Will bring Yahweh on you and on your people and on [the] house of your father days which not have come from [the] day of [the] departing of Ephraim from with Judah, the king of Assyria.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring days on you, on your people, and on your royal house that have not been seen since Ephraim split off from Judah: the king of Assyria!

L.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring upon you and upon your people and upon the house of your father days which have not come since the day Ephraim departed from Judah: the king of Assyria.

R.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring hard times on you, your people, and your royal family. There have been no days like them since the northern tribes split away from Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring the king of Assyria against you.

decisions.choice: days which have not come: a time of disaster, which the king of Assyria will bring
alternatives: days of blessing such as have not been since the division
decisions.reason: The phrase alone could mean days of blessing, but the closing words, "the king of Assyria", show what kind of days they are: the power Ahaz looked to for help will become the threat (8:7-8). The Assyrian king of Ahaz's day was Tiglath-pileser III (2 Kings 16:7).

decisions.choice: since Ephraim departed from Judah: since the kingdom split
decisions.reason: After Solomon's death the northern tribes broke away from David's line and made Jeroboam their king (1 Kings 12:16-20), about two hundred years before Ahaz.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria: added at the end to name the disaster
decisions.reason: The words stand at the end of the sentence, after the description of the days, and name what those days will bring.

decisions.choice: hard times ... will bring the king of Assyria against you
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of days are meant and makes "the king of Assyria" a sentence of its own. It calls Ephraim "the northern tribes".

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ לַזְּב֔וּב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה יְאֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלַ֨דְּבוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day the that, will whistle Yahweh for the fly which [is] at [the] end of [the] streams of Egypt and for the bee which [is] in [the] land of Assyria.
pieces: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will whistle for the fly from the farthest streams of Egypt and for the bee in the land of Assyria.

L.18: And it will be in that day, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will whistle for the fly that [is] at the end of the streams of Egypt and for the bee that [is] in the land of Assyria.

R.18: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will whistle to call armies from Egypt and Assyria. They will come like flies from the far-off streams of Egypt and like bees from the land of Assyria.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will whistle: God calls the nations as easily as one calls an animal
decisions.reason: In 5:26 God whistles for a nation from the ends of the earth, and it comes quickly. The great powers come when God calls them.

decisions.choice: the fly ... the bee: armies swarming in
decisions.reason: Flies and bees stand for the armies of Egypt and Assyria, countless and stinging (compare Deuteronomy 1:44). The "streams of Egypt" are the channels of the Nile, and "the end" of them is the far south of Egypt.

decisions.choice: to call armies ... They will come like flies ... like bees
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the flies and bees are pictures of armies.

records.heading: The fly and the bee

records.source: וּבָ֨אוּ וְנָח֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ בְּנַחֲלֵ֣י הַבַּתּ֔וֹת וּבִנְקִיקֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִ֑ים וּבְכֹל֙ הַנַּ֣עֲצוּצִ֔ים וּבְכֹ֖ל הַנַּהֲלֹלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they will come and they will settle, all of them, in [the] ravines of the steep places and in [the] clefts of the rocks and on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.
pieces: They will all swarm in and settle in the gorges under the cliffs and in the cracks of the rocks, on every thorny shrub and at every place where the flocks drink.

L.19: And they will come and settle, all of them, in the ravines of the steep places and in the clefts of the rocks, and on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.

R.19: All of them will come and settle everywhere: in deep valleys, in cracks in the rocks, on every thornbush, and at every place where animals drink.

decisions.choice: watering places: places where flocks drink
decisions.reason: The word is found only here, and its sense is uncertain. It most likely means a watering place for animals; it may instead mean a pasture.

decisions.choice: ravines, clefts, thornbushes, watering places: everywhere
decisions.reason: Like a swarm settling on every surface, the invaders will fill the land, from the wild places to the places where flocks are tended. There will be nowhere to hide (compare 2:19-21).

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יְגַלַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָי֩ בְּתַ֨עַר הַשְּׂכִירָ֜ה בְּעֶבְרֵ֤י נָהָר֙ בְּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר אֶת־הָרֹ֖אשׁ וְשַׂ֣עַר הָרַגְלָ֑יִםוְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַזָּקָ֖ן תִּסְפֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: In the day the that, will shave [the] Lord with a razor the hired in [the] regions beyond [the] River, with [the] king of Assyria, the head and [the] hair of the feet, and also the beard it will sweep away.
pieces: On that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor from beyond the Euphrates, the king of Assyria. He will shave the head and the hair of the body, and it will strip away the beard as well.

L.20: In that day the Lord will shave with the razor hired from beyond the River, with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet, and it will also sweep away the beard.

R.20: At that time the Lord will use the king of Assyria like a hired razor from beyond the Euphrates River. He will shave the heads and bodies of the people of Judah, and even their beards. It will be a terrible disgrace.

decisions.choice: shaving the head and beard: shame and defeat
decisions.reason: To have one's beard shaved by another was a deep disgrace (2 Samuel 10:4-5), and captives might be shaved and stripped. The picture is of Judah humiliated and stripped bare by the invader.

decisions.choice: the hair of the feet: the hair of the body
alternatives: the hair of the private parts
decisions.reason: "Feet" here most likely means the legs and lower body, and it may be a polite way to speak of the private parts, as "feet" sometimes is (compare Judges 3:24). With the head and beard, it means the whole body is shaved.

decisions.choice: a hired razor from beyond the River: the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Euphrates, which lay between Judah and Assyria. Ahaz paid the king of Assyria with silver and gold from the temple to come and help him (2 Kings 16:7-8); the one he hired will be the razor God uses against Judah.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates / the hair of the body / the people of Judah ... It will be a terrible disgrace.
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Euphrates and say "body" for "feet". Readable says whose heads are shaved and states the shame the picture means.

records.source: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא יְחַיֶּה־אִ֛ישׁ עֶגְלַ֥ת בָּקָ֖ר וּשְׁתֵּי־צֹֽאן׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day the that, will keep alive a man a heifer of [the] herd and two sheep.
pieces: On that day someone will keep a heifer and two sheep alive.

L.21: And it will be in that day, a man will keep alive a heifer of the herd and two sheep.

R.21: At that time a person will keep just one young cow and two sheep.

decisions.choice: will keep alive a heifer and two sheep: a household reduced to a few animals
decisions.reason: After the invasion a family will have only a young cow and a couple of sheep or goats left. The next verse shows the other side: with so few people, these animals will have pasture enough to give plenty of milk.

decisions.choice: sheep: animals of the flock
decisions.reason: The word means animals of the flock, sheep or goats.

decisions.choice: just one
decisions.reason: Readable says "just one" to show how little is left, as the context implies.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה מֵרֹ֛ב עֲשׂ֥וֹת חָלָ֖ב יֹאכַ֣ל חֶמְאָ֑ה כִּֽי־חֶמְאָ֤ה וּדְבַשׁ֙ יֹאכֵ֔ל כָּל־הַנּוֹתָ֖ר בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, from [the] abundance of producing milk he will eat curds, for curds and honey will eat every one who is left in [the] midst of the land.
pieces: They will give so much milk that he will have curds to eat; indeed, curds and honey will be the food of all who are left in the land.

L.22: And it will be, from the abundance of producing milk he will eat curds, for curds and honey every one who is left in the midst of the land will eat.

R.22: They will give plenty of milk, so he will have curds to eat. All the people still left in the land will live on curds and honey.

decisions.choice: plenty of milk, curds and honey: the food of herders in an emptied land
decisions.reason: With so few people and so much unworked land, a few animals give more milk than a family needs. People will live on milk and wild honey instead of grain and wine. This explains the curds and honey of verse 15.

decisions.choice: every one who is left: those who survive
decisions.reason: Only a remnant will remain in the land, as the name of Isaiah's son had said (verse 3). They will have enough, but the land will no longer be farmed.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִֽהְיֶ֣ה כָל־מָק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִֽהְיֶה־שָּׁ֛ם אֶ֥לֶף גֶּ֖פֶן בְּאֶ֣לֶף כָּ֑סֶף לַשָּׁמִ֥יר וְלַשַּׁ֖יִת יִֽהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day the that, will be every place where there was there a thousand vines for a thousand [of] silver, for thorns and for briers it will be.
pieces: On that day every vineyard of a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be overrun by thorns and briers.

L.23: And it will be in that day, every place where there were a thousand vines, [worth] a thousand [pieces of] silver, will become thorns and briers.

R.23: At that time, every vineyard that had a thousand grapevines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be covered with thorns and briers.

decisions.choice: a thousand vines for a thousand silver: the best vineyards
decisions.reason: A thousand vines worth a thousand pieces of silver, probably shekels, a silver coin for each vine, describes a large and valuable vineyard (compare Song of Songs 8:11). Even the richest land will go wild.

decisions.choice: thorns and briers: the vineyard left to ruin
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes God's vineyard left unpruned and unhoed in 5:6, and they come back in 9:17, 10:17 and 27:4.

records.source: בַּחִצִּ֥ים וּבַקֶּ֖שֶׁת יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה כִּי־שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: With arrows and with bow one will come there, for thorns and briers will be all the land.
pieces: Anyone who goes there will carry a bow and arrows, for thorns and briers will cover the whole land.

L.24: With arrows and with bow one will go there, for all the land will be thorns and briers.

R.24: People will have to carry bows and arrows when they go there, because the whole land will be covered with thorns and briers.

decisions.choice: with arrows and bow: the land has become wild country
alternatives: people must go armed against wild animals
decisions.reason: Farmland will turn into wild, overgrown country, entered only by hunters or by people armed against wild animals. The verse does not say which; either way, no one will farm it.

records.source: וְכֹ֣ל הֶהָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּמַּעְדֵּר֙ יֵעָ֣דֵר֔וּן לֹֽא־תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְהָיָה֙ לְמִשְׁלַ֣ח שׁ֔וֹר וּלְמִרְמַ֖ס שֶֽׂה׃פ
records.gloss: And all the hills which with the hoe they were hoed, not you will go there [for] fear of thorns and briers; and it will be for a sending-out of ox and a trampling-place of sheep.
pieces: As for the hills that used to be worked with the hoe, you will not go to them for fear of the thorns and briers. Oxen will be let out to graze there, and sheep will trample the ground."

L.25: And all the hills which were hoed with the hoe, you will not go there [for] fear of thorns and briers; and it will be for a place where oxen are sent out and a trampling place of sheep."

R.25: People used to dig the soil on the hills with hoes. But no one will go there anymore, because they will be afraid of the thorns and briers. Cattle and sheep will be let loose there to graze and trample the ground."

decisions.choice: you will not go there for fear of thorns and briers
alternatives: the fear of thorns and briers will not come there
decisions.reason: The verb can be read "you will go" or "it will come". If the second, the sense is that "the fear of thorns and briers will not come there": the hills once worked with the hoe will stay clear of thorns but become pasture. The first reading fits the picture of verses 23-24, where thorns cover the land.

decisions.choice: a place where oxen are let loose and sheep trample: farmland turned to pasture
decisions.reason: The hills that were once dug and planted will be left to the animals. Isaiah's prophecy against Judah's vineyard ends in the same way (5:5-6).

decisions.choice: no one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here means anyone; Readable says "no one".
